core.title: Haul-out at Harborline stands
core.setting: A tailor of sails at Windward Sails whose assistant keeps boat measurements, repair jobs, and seasonal haul-out bookings

events.text: Standing rule for the workshop: once a haul-out booking for a client's boat is confirmed, we never move it to another date or another yard without that boat owner's written agreement. The booking stays as made until they say otherwise.
Standing rule: any supplier order above 800 in total needs sign-off from Pieter, our finance lead, before it goes out. Below that I can order on my own judgement.
Kestrel is a 34-foot sloop owned by Dana Ortiz. She keeps her at Harborline Marina and her best contact is her email; she is quick to reply. Dana is one of our longest-standing sail clients.

Our autumn travelift schedule for Windward Sails clients: lift slots run Mondays and Thursdays through October, hard-stand is 340 per day, and the week we can offer you opens on Monday 12 October 2026. Boats need a valid insurance certificate on file before lifting.

Booked the seasonal haul-out for Dana Ortiz's sloop Kestrel at Harborline Marina: travelift lift on Monday 12 October 2026, five days on the hard at their daily hard-stand rate of 340. Dana knows the plan.
Quotation for Dacron sailcloth, weight 8 oz: 96 per metre, sold in 20-metre bolts. Price holds for the season.
Ordered three 20-metre bolts of 8 oz Dacron from Fairwind Textiles at their quoted 96 per metre for the Kestrel mainsail recut. Well under the 800 sign-off line, so no need to bother Pieter.
Re-measured the mainsail as asked: luff 11.6 metres, foot 4.2 metres, leech 12.1 metres. Same numbers as two seasons ago, so use these for the recut.

Scheduled the Kestrel mainsail recut in the loft for Tuesday 13 October 2026, the day after the haul-out lift, using the Fairwind Dacron and Dana's measurements (luff 11.6 m, foot 4.2 m). Assigned to Tomas in the loft.
Booked a dockside measure visit for Kestrel's new jib at Harborline Marina, dock 5, on Friday 28 August 2026. I will take the tape and Dana's contact details along; she keeps the boat there.
Loft floor is clear after the summer rush. I have the Kestrel job on the board for the second week of October; nothing else booked that week so far.
Workshop van service is booked for Thursday 1 October 2026, so the van is off the road that day only. For any marina runs around the haul-out week the van is free as usual.

Yard rules reminder: every boat lifted by our travelift must have a current insurance certificate on file with the yard before the lift date. Please make sure your clients' paperwork is in order for the October week.
To do: get Dana Ortiz's insurance certificate for Kestrel to Harborline before 5 October 2026.
Insurance certificate for Kestrel is attached — sent it on to the yard office myself this morning. Everything set for the lift?

We now run a travelift service for sailmakers' clients from our own yard: lift slots available from 5 October 2026 onward at 290 per day hard-stand. We are three miles up the coast from Harborline and happy to take overflow work. Give us a call if useful.
Confirming your yard week: Kestrel is on the travelift list for Monday 12 October 2026, five days on the hard. Insurance certificate received, thank you.
Just to flag again: our travelift still has open slots for the week of Monday 19 October 2026 at 290 per day, if any of your clients' boats need lifting. Easy to add a boat at short notice.
Called to say the lift went smoothly this morning and the boat is sitting on the hard. Looking forward to the recut tomorrow.
Quarterly books look fine. Fairwind invoice for the three bolts came in as quoted. Nothing needing sign-off this month.
Kestrel recut went well on Tuesday; sail is flaked and ready to go back on the boat. I left the Fairwind offcuts on the shelf as usual.
